This optimization speeds up object creation significantly, especially with keyword parameters, and improves cache efficiency, marking a notable performance boost in Ruby's runtime.

headline: Transpiler is a meaningless word (2023)
short_description: Transpilers are often misunderstood; they are complex tools that involve semantic transformations similar to compilers. Many claim they are simple syntax converters, but in reality, they handle intricate language features, semantics, and backend processes, blurring the line between transpilers and traditional compilers.

headline: Compiling OCaml to the TI-84+ CE Calculator
short_description: A developer has created a method to compile OCaml code to run on a TI-84+ CE calculator by leveraging Js_of_ocaml to generate portable C code. This approach involves building a custom C backend, implementing a simple garbage collector, and integrating with OCaml’s build system, enabling OCaml programs to run on small devices like calculators.

headline: How the jax.jit() JIT compiler works in jax-js
short_description: A developer is building jax-js, a lightweight deep learning compiler in JavaScript inspired by XLA and Tinygrad. It aims to enable efficient browser-based numerical computing and GPU acceleration, with plans to support jax.jit() and optimize performance for web ML applications.

headline: Inline Your Runtime
short_description: A new approach enables embedding a custom runtime directly into a Rust-based compiler using LLVM bitcode, allowing for whole-program optimization, safer runtime, and easier testing. Despite workflow limitations and dependency on matching LLVM versions, this method offers improved performance and portability for language implementation.

headline: A JavaScript library for building parsers, interpreters, compilers, and more
short_description: Ohm is a JavaScript parsing toolkit leveraging PEGs, enabling developers to build custom parsers, interpreters, and compilers. Its modular design, support for left recursion, and online visualization tools make it ideal for creating flexible language tools and educational programming environments.

headline: Evolution of Rust compiler errors
short_description: Rust compiler error messages have significantly improved over time, with versions introducing colorful displays, error codes, and helpful explanations. This evolution reflects decades of dedicated effort by numerous contributors, enhancing developer experience and debugging clarity.

headline: A leap year check in three instructions
short_description: Researchers developed a highly optimized, bit-twiddling leap year check that reduces the calculation to three instructions using precomputed constants and bit masking techniques. Although complex, this method offers significant speedups over traditional modulo-based approaches, especially in predictable input scenarios.

headline: ZJIT has been merged into Ruby
short_description: Ruby's ZJIT, a new JIT compiler built into YARV, has been merged into Ruby, offering a more traditional compiler architecture with high-level IR and modular optimization. While still early in development, ZJIT aims to improve performance and correctness, complementing the existing YJIT in Ruby 3.5.

headline: bold linker v0.2.0 release - bold just got faster
short_description: Bold v0.2.0 boosts linking speeds by over 19%, outperforming previous versions and surpassing LLD, though still behind Apple's ld64. The update includes performance improvements and dependency upgrades, enhancing build efficiency.

headline: 200 and change
short_description: A collection of compact, powerful code examples showcases concepts like packrat parsing, virtual DOM, and relational databases in about 250 lines, inviting community contributions to expand or annotate the demos.

headline: Beating the fastest lexer generator in Rust (2023)
short_description: A Rust lexer implementation using logos outperforms a naive approach, achieving nearly twice the speed on ARM architectures through techniques like SIMD, ASCII dispatch, and inlining. Optimizations such as perfect hash functions and table lookups further enhance performance, with results showing at least a 20% throughput improvement over existing solutions.

headline: Starting on seamless C++ interop in jank
short_description: Jank has made significant progress in enabling seamless C++ interop, including accessing C++ values, constructors, and casting, using LLVM IR and Clang. The project aims to support complex C++ features and headers, with ongoing work to handle function calls, member access, and destructors, promising powerful integration with C++ code.

headline: An Apple Library Primer
short_description: Apple’s Mach-O file format supports multiple platform architectures, dynamic libraries, frameworks, and universal binaries, with recent updates introducing mergeable libraries and static frameworks in Xcode 15. The format's tools and concepts, including code signing, symbol management, and position independence, remain complex but essential for app development and optimization.

headline: Designing type inference for high quality type errors
short_description: The article advocates for improved type inference error messages, highlighting that current languages often produce inscrutable errors due to design choices like guesswork, overloading, and lack of explicit annotations. It introduces PolySubML’s approach, emphasizing clear error reporting, user clarifications, and explicit annotations to enhance debugging, arguing that high-quality errors are achievable without sacrificing powerful inference.

headline: An i386 Hobby operating system with graphics, multitasking, networking and an i386 C compiler
short_description: A new hobby OS for the i386 platform, RetrOS-32, offers graphics, multitasking, networking, and an i386 C compiler, showcasing advanced capabilities for retro computing enthusiasts.

headline: Co-dfns versus BQN's implementation
short_description: Recent advances highlight that array-based compilers like BQN and Co-dfns are competitive with traditional scalar compilers on CPUs, with potential for GPU acceleration. While promising, current data-parallel methods face challenges in implementing complex optimizations, and GPU compilers remain limited by fundamental issues like register allocation and syntax complexity.

headline: The world of compiler backends
short_description: Compiler backends play a crucial role in translating intermediate code into optimized machine code for evolving architectures, presenting ongoing challenges in supporting new features and hardware. As they adapt to hardware advancements and language changes, working on backends offers continuous innovation and career growth in the tech field.

headline: GCC 15.1 Released
short_description: GCC 15.1, a major release, introduces new features including C23 and C++26 support, experimental modules in libstdc++, and enhanced vectorization. Developers highlight improvements and porting notes, with the update available on official servers for download.

headline: GPU Compilation with MLIR
short_description: This article details a comprehensive pipeline for compiling high-level MLIR tensor operations into NVIDIA GPU-compatible code. It covers lowering MLIR to PTX via multiple transformation passes, generating PTX with LLVM tools, and executing kernels through Python bindings with CUDA driver APIs. The process enables dynamic, optimized GPU kernel generation from abstract tensor expressions.

headline: Detecting if an expression is constant in C
short_description: Overcoming challenges in C macro design, developers explore multiple methods—like constexpr, __builtin_constant_p, static_assert, and array-based tricks—to detect compile-time constants, balancing compatibility and type integrity. These techniques aim to ensure expressions are constant at compile time across various C standards.

headline: Flambda2 Ep. 4: How to write a purely functional compiler
short_description: OCamlPro discusses the design of Flambda2, an optimizing compiler for OCaml that uses CPS representation. It employs two-pass traversals—downward for analysis and inline, and upward for dead code elimination—enabling efficient, single-pass code transformation despite CPS complexities.

headline: What the Hell Is a Target Triple?
short_description: Target triples in compilers are complex, inconsistent strings representing architecture, vendor, OS, and ABI. LLVM dominates current naming conventions, but the system remains organic and often confusing, with many variants and aliases especially for ARM and x86 architectures. Creating new triples is discouraged due to their chaotic nature.

headline: Building LLVM plugins with Bazel
short_description: This article details how to build LLVM plugins with Bazel, focusing on supporting multiple LLVM versions across OSes. It covers dynamically detecting installed versions, defining repositories, and creating build and test targets, ensuring reproducible and flexible plugin development.

headline: awe: A compiler for the Algol W programming language
short_description: Glynawe/awe is a new compiler for the Algol W programming language, but users are currently unable to perform actions on the repository.

headline: Python Performance: Why 'if not list' is 2x Faster Than Using len()
short_description: Python’s “if not mylist” check is roughly twice as fast as using “len() == 0” due to internal optimizations. The latter involves function calls and multiple pointer dereferences, while the former benefits from CPython's instruction specialization, directly accessing the list size in its header for quick emptiness testing.

headline: Rust to C compiler - 95.9% test pass rate, odd platforms
short_description: The developer reports progress on their Rust-to-C compiler, achieving a 95.9% test pass rate, fixing bugs in 128-bit intrinsics, subslicing, and overflow checks. They aim for better platform support and performance improvements, while exploring IR optimizations and compatibility with obscure C compilers to expand Rust's reach across diverse systems.

headline: 6 usability improvements in GCC 15
short_description: GCC 15 introduces major usability upgrades, including improved error diagnostics with nesting, color highlighting, and machine-readable SARIF output. It also offers better C++ template error messages, more flexible diagnostics outputs, and supports C23 by default, enhancing developer experience and debugging clarity.

headline: Doing the Prospero-Challenge in RPython
short_description: The author explored optimizing the Prospero Challenge's rendering process using interval analysis, peephole rules, and demand-driven sign analysis. Rewriting in C and leveraging SIMD improved performance, with the demanded info optimization providing notable speed gains. Extensive testing ensured correctness, highlighting the potential for further enhancements.

headline: GSoC 2024: The 1001 thresholds in LLVM
short_description: GSoC 2024's LLVM project investigates how varying thresholds impact performance metrics like compile-time and code size. Using a new tool, researchers found that optimal threshold values are file-specific, highlighting the need for adaptive mechanisms to improve LLVM optimization.

headline: A surprising enum size optimization in the Rust compiler
short_description: Rust's compiler performs an unexpected size optimization for nested enums, making some enum variants occupy less memory than their payloads suggest. For example, `Option<char>` uses only 4 bytes instead of 8, leveraging niche optimization. Similarly, nested enums like `Outer` and `Inner` are represented more compactly, often sharing payload space and reducing overall memory footprint.

headline: How Does C Code Become Assembly
short_description: LLVM IR is a simplified, assembly-like intermediate representation that uses registers, control-flow graphs, and SSA form to optimize code translation from C. It handles conditionals, loops, and data types explicitly, facilitating efficient compilation to x86-64 assembly with clear register and memory management.

headline: Global Value Numbering Using Random Interpretation
short_description: Researchers introduce a polynomial-time randomized algorithm for global value numbering, leveraging random interpretation techniques. The method simplifies implementation but admits a small probability of false equality, which can be minimized with parameter adjustments.

headline: "Verified" "Compilation" of "Python" with Knuckledragger, GCC, and Ghidra
short_description: This article explores advanced techniques for formal verification and symbolic analysis of binary code using tools like Ghidra, Angr, and SMT solvers. It discusses integrating assembly semantics, creating verified interpreters, and challenges in handling symbolic memory models, highlighting ongoing efforts to achieve more rigorous, automated binary verification workflows.

headline: Making a Brainf*** JIT Compiler in Rust
short_description: A new project demonstrates building a Brainf*** JIT compiler using Rust, showcasing advanced programming techniques and potentially improving performance for esoteric languages.

headline: When should a compiler expand garbage collection barriers?
short_description: A production compiler (C2) in the JDK has shifted from early to late garbage collection barrier expansion for G1, reducing compilation overhead and complexity. Despite concerns about performance loss, preliminary results show no significant degradation, highlighting trade-offs between optimization and maintainability in compiler design.

headline: JIT calculators finale
short_description: The final installment of the JIT calculator challenge showcases reader solutions, including hand-rolled machine code generators and library-based approaches like Cranelift. Participants explored low-level code generation, highlighting Cranelift’s portability and optimization features, and demonstrate ongoing interest in JIT compilation projects.

headline: Compilers: Incrementally and Extensibly
short_description: A practical course on compiler construction guides students in building a complete x86-64 compiler for the Tiger language using OCaml. Emphasizing incremental development, extensibility, and modern software practices, the course incorporates custom build tools and focuses on understanding parsing, type-checking, optimization, and assembly generation.

headline: A Simple Reply
short_description: Twitch has banned gambling sites following a scammer's $200,000 fraud, prompting some streamers to consider boycotting the platform amid concerns over safety and trust.

headline: Making OCaml Safe for Performance Engineering
short_description: Google Chrome plans to phase out support for Adobe Flash by the end of 2020, encouraging users to transition to more secure, modern web standards. The move aims to improve security and performance across the browser ecosystem.

headline: Prospero with Cranelift JIT and SIMD
short_description: A Rust-based JIT compiler using Cranelift has been optimized for SIMD vectorization, boosting rendering performance from 5 seconds to under 300ms for 1024x1024 images. Despite Cranelift's current limitations with wider vectors, vectorized IR and parallel processing significantly accelerate pixel calculations, demonstrating impressive gains with relatively low effort.

headline: Fast Compilation or Fast Execution: Just Have Both
short_description: CedarDB leverages JIT code generation to optimize query performance by creating custom machine code tailored to data structures and queries. This approach combines the flexibility of interpretation with the speed of hand-written code, achieving throughput comparable to manually optimized implementations while maintaining adaptability for diverse workloads.

headline: Baseline implementations should be predictable
short_description: Reciprocal offers a predictable, efficient approach to integer division by constants, executing at about 1.3 ns per division compared to 9.6 ns for hardware division, with consistent performance across divisors. Its unified code path avoids branching, simplifying implementation and ensuring steady performance regardless of divisor complexity.

headline: Labor of Division (2010)
short_description: This article explains how to optimize unsigned integer division by using precomputed "magic numbers" to replace costly division operations with multiplication and shifts. It details the process of selecting the smallest suitable magic number, how to handle special cases, and potential improvements for specific divisors, making division faster on fixed-point hardware.

headline: Can jank beat Clojure's error reporting?
short_description: Jank, a new Lisp-focused project, aims to surpass Clojure in error reporting by providing precise source info, highlighted code snippets, and detailed notes, even through macro expansions. The developer highlights ongoing improvements, especially in handling source tracking and macro analysis, with plans for enhanced C++ interop.

headline: Data demand some damn respect
short_description: The article explores a simplified approach to web computing and data serialization, advocating for flat scraps and scrapscript to improve efficiency, sharing, and maintainability. It emphasizes using common serialization formats like CBOR/MsgPack, referencing data via hashes, and developing minimalist, high-level languages like scrapscript for better software simplicity and performance.

headline: Calculate Throughput with LLVM's Scheduling Model
short_description: LLVM’s scheduling model allows calculation of instruction inverse throughput by analyzing AcquireAtCycle and ReleaseAtCycle metrics, especially for instructions with resource segments. The key is identifying the maximum segment length or the right-most cycle, which dominates throughput, even when instructions have non-zero acquire times.

headline: SJS: a static AOT compiler for a subset of JavaScript (2016)
short_description: Samsung’s SJS is a static AOT compiler targeting a subset of JavaScript, aiming to improve performance and reliability for specific applications.

headline: Go’s FIPS 140-3 Compliance
short_description: Go 1.24 introduces native FIPS 140-3 compliance, enabling cryptographic modules to meet U.S. government standards. The update includes self-checks and support for approved algorithms, with optional modes for strict compliance, enhancing security for government and enterprise applications.

headline: Go Cryptography Security Audit
short_description: Google's Go team completed a security audit of its cryptography packages, revealing a low-severity issue in legacy code and some informational findings. They confirmed a robust security track record and are developing a native FIPS 140-3 mode, alongside plans for post-quantum cryptography and simplified high-level APIs.

headline: The cryptography behind passkeys
short_description: Passkeys utilize cryptographic key pairs and WebAuthn to offer phishing-resistant, passwordless authentication. They enhance security by origin binding and support extensions for advanced cryptographic functions, though their security depends on proper implementation and authenticators. Support for passkeys is growing, promising a more secure future for web authentication.

headline: A New Kali Linux Archive Signing Key
short_description: Kali Linux has introduced a new signing key after losing access to the previous one, causing apt update failures. Users must manually download and install the new key to continue updates, with updated images now including the new keyring.

headline: What the heck is AEAD again?
short_description: AEAD (Authenticated Encryption with Associated Data) is now industry standard, providing both encryption and authentication in a single API. It helps prevent common cryptographic mistakes, especially when handling unencrypted associated data, with libraries like libsodium simplifying secure implementation across various applications.

headline: Audit of the Rust p256 Crate
short_description: NEAR's security audit of the p256 crate found no major issues, highlighting its thorough testing and architecture for elliptic curve operations. The report details the implementation of P-256, Montgomery and Barrett reductions, and point encoding, emphasizing the importance of constant-time algorithms and efficient arithmetic for cryptographic security.

headline: McEliece standardization
short_description: NIST's 2025 report highlights ongoing standardization efforts for Classic McEliece, emphasizing its strong security track record and small ciphertexts, especially for static keys. Despite delays and some misrepresentations, many experts advocate for adopting McEliece due to its proven resilience, small size, and suitability for applications with limited bandwidth.

headline: 15,000 lines of verified cryptography now in Python
short_description: Python has integrated 15,000 lines of verified cryptographic code from HACL* into its core, enhancing security and correctness for hash and streaming APIs. This major update involved overcoming complex build, memory, and abstraction challenges, marking a significant milestone for verified cryptography in mainstream software.

headline: Intuiting TLS
short_description: TLS encrypts web communication through key exchange, encryption, and authentication techniques like Diffie-Hellman, hash functions, and certificates issued by trusted authorities. This complex infrastructure ensures privacy, data integrity, and verifies the identity of websites, forming the backbone of secure internet browsing.

headline: How To Become A Hacker: A Step-By-Step Guide
short_description: A detailed guide explores how to become a hacker, emphasizing skills like mastering Vim, understanding DNS and DNSSEC, and targeting the vulnerabilities in centralized internet infrastructure. The narrative reveals a desire to decentralize web control, driven by personal motives and a background in white-hat hacking.

headline: Operationalizing Macaroons
short_description: Fly.io’s engineers detail their extensive use of Macaroon bearer tokens for secure, scalable API authentication and authorization. They highlight innovations in token management, revocation, caching, and security, emphasizing how Macaroons enhance infrastructure reliability and security while supporting internal automation and traceability.

headline: The Practical Limitations of End-to-End Encryption
short_description: End-to-end encryption (E2EE) ensures message privacy between endpoints but doesn't protect against scams or meet military standards like SCIFs. Experts emphasize that Signal and similar apps are not suitable for classified communications, and encryption's primary role remains safeguarding privacy, not establishing trust or security in all contexts.

headline: Entropy Attacks (2014)
short_description: Entropy attacks reveal that malicious entropy sources can manipulate cryptographic outputs, including signatures and keys, by controlling just a few bits. Experts advocate for deterministic, pre-generated keys and minimizing entropy input during cryptographic operations to enhance security and prevent covert communication channels.

headline: CDC attack mitigation in Plakar
short_description: Plakar released version 1.0.1-beta.13, introducing features like enhanced UI filtering, snapshot timeline, transfer checkpointing, FTP export, improved S3 support, and performance optimizations such as B+tree caching and parallelized check/restore. The update also addresses security concerns related to CDC attacks with new mitigation techniques.

headline: Failing upwards: the Twitter encrypted DM failure
short_description: Twitter’s encrypted DMs, launched nearly two years ago, suffer from significant security and functionality flaws, including key management issues, lack of forward secrecy, and no group chat support. Despite the technical simplicity of encryption, Twitter’s implementation remains incomplete and unaddressed, unlike Signal’s robust solution.

headline: Zero-Knowledge Proofs
short_description: A browser update alert appeared on YouTube, urging users to upgrade to the latest versions of Firefox, Chrome, Opera, or Edge for optimal experience and new features.

headline: Constant-Time Code: The Pessimist Case
short_description: A new paper warns that writing truly constant-time cryptographic code is increasingly challenging, suggesting failures due to timing side-channels may become more common as implementation complexity grows, potentially making secure software development infeasible in the future.

headline: RPMB, a secret place inside the eMMC
short_description: The RPMB (Replay Protected Memory Block) partition in eMMC provides secure, authenticated storage for sensitive data, preventing replay and downgrade attacks. Accessible via Linux, RPMB uses a one-time programmable key, counters, and HMAC SHA-256 to ensure data integrity, making it vital for secure device operations like firmware updates and digital rights management.

headline: Can I use Secure Curves in the Web Platform?
short_description: Efforts to integrate Ed25519 and X25519 algorithms into the Web Cryptography API have advanced across major browsers, improving security and interoperability. Despite delays in Chrome due to spec disagreements, Firefox and WebKit now support these algorithms by default, marking a significant step toward a more secure, decentralized web platform.

headline: MLS is Coming to Wire App
short_description: Wire is deploying MLS (Messaging Layer Security) to enhance encryption and support larger group chats, starting March 2025. The upgrade improves security but requires users to update their apps and devices, as older versions and unsupported devices will no longer be compatible.

headline: Noir programming language
short_description: Noir is a domain-specific programming language aimed at private and verifiable computing, allowing developers to create concise proofs of program execution. Influenced by Rust, it supports SNARK proving systems and emphasizes a simple, familiar syntax for secure, transparent computations.

headline: bad apple but it's ssh keys
short_description: A complex script generates SSH key-based visual art from video frames, converting images into ASCII characters and creating animated terminal output. It employs Rust code to optimize key fingerprints for artistic rendering, with plans to automate video splitting, frame conversion, and final reassembly.

headline: Three questions about Apple, encryption, and the U.K
short_description: The U.K.’s secret order to weaken Apple’s end-to-end encryption raises concerns over privacy and security, prompting Apple to disable its encrypted iCloud backup for U.K. users. This move highlights the legal and ethical challenges tech companies face amid government demands for backdoors into user data.

headline: Ring is unmaintained
short_description: Ring, an open-source library, is currently unmaintained due to its author’s indefinite hiatus, raising concerns over security vulnerabilities. The rustls team has stepped in to provide security-only maintenance, restoring some stability to its development.

headline: How to prove false statements? (Part 1)
short_description: Cryptography experts highlight that schemes proven secure in the random oracle model may be insecure when instantiated with real hash functions like SHA-2. As cryptographic protocols grow more complex, especially with recursive zero-knowledge proofs, the risk of hidden backdoors and cross-program vulnerabilities increases, raising concerns about future system security.

headline: Reviewing the Cryptography Used by Signal
short_description: A cryptography expert reviews Signal’s security, emphasizing the importance of audits and transparency. He highlights Signal’s robust cryptographic features, including key transparency and forward-secure protocols, and discusses the limitations of security audits, aiming to help users understand applied cryptography and assess privacy claims effectively.

headline: Accelerating The Adoption of Post-Quantum Cryptography with PHP
short_description: NIST has published initial standards for Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC), prompting efforts to integrate these algorithms into PHP to boost widespread adoption. This move aims to future-proof web security, enable end-to-end encrypted messaging, and facilitate the implementation of new protocols like MLS and PASETO in PHP applications.

headline: A Brief History of Code Signing at Mozilla
short_description: Mozilla's code signing process has evolved over 20 years from manual signing to an automated, secure system using tools like Autograph and chain of trust. Recent advancements include signing via Linux servers, cloud notarization, and support for macOS and Windows artifacts, significantly improving speed and security.

headline: Running Private DeepSeek R1 with Verifiable Security
short_description: Tinfoil has launched DeepSeek R1-70B with verifiable security, offering private AI chat through confidential computing and hardware security layers. This breakthrough aims to address privacy concerns in AI, ensuring user data remains exclusively accessible to the user, not service providers or third parties.

headline: Hell Is Overconfident Developers Writing Encryption Code
short_description: Cryptography experts warn that many developers overestimate their understanding, leading to insecure custom encryption implementations. The industry continues to see risks from unreviewed, "homegrown" cryptography, emphasizing the need for trustworthy tools and expert oversight to prevent costly security mistakes.

headline: How we share secrets at a fully-remote startup
short_description: A remote startup’s co-CEO shares how they securely handle secrets using simple, trusted tools like Node.js, avoiding complex or untrusted encryption software. By building a small, transparent script leveraging open-source cryptography, they enable encrypted sharing of API keys while maintaining security and understanding.

headline: Best practices for key derivation
short_description: Key derivation must be used carefully to maintain security. Best practices include using HKDF with proper salts, unique info values, and avoiding low-entropy inputs or hash functions as KDFs. Combining keys should rely on dual PRFs like HMAC, and leveraging established protocols can often replace custom KDF solutions.

headline: EU's Digital Identity Systems - Reality Check and Techniques for Better Privacy
short_description: EU's digital identity systems face scrutiny over privacy concerns, prompting calls for improved techniques to safeguard user data amid ongoing adoption efforts.

headline: Private Keys in the Fortigate Leak
short_description: A recent leak of Fortinet configuration files reveals thousands of encrypted private keys and certificates, many still vulnerable due to static encryption keys and default passwords. Despite known exploits since 2022, most affected users have not replaced or revoked compromised keys, highlighting ongoing security risks.

headline: Radical CS
short_description: NIST's Third Workshop on Block Cipher Modes of Operation took place October 3-4, 2023, at NCCoE in Rockville, MD, featuring a keynote by UC Davis's Phillip Rogaway on the latest developments in cryptographic security and encryption standards.

headline: Verified post-quantum cryptography on the web
short_description: Google's new research introduces verified post-quantum cryptography for web security, highlighting the need for quantum-resistant protocols. While current browsers like Chrome and Firefox are not yet PQ-ready, efforts are underway to implement secure quantum-proof algorithms.

headline: How We Cracked a 512-Bit DKIM Key for Less Than $8 in the Cloud
short_description: Researchers demonstrated that a 512-bit RSA DKIM key can be cracked in under 86 hours for less than $8 using cloud computing, highlighting the insecurity of short keys. They successfully forged DKIM signatures that passed certain email providers’ checks, urging domain owners to upgrade to 1,024-bit keys for security.

headline: The GPU, not the TPM, is the root of hardware DRM
short_description: The FSF claims that TPMs are central to hardware DRM, but experts clarify that DRM relies on GPU-based encryption, not TPMs. TPMs are too slow and limited for media decryption, and industry-standard DRM like Playready functions effectively without TPMs, undermining the FSF’s argument.

headline: Colliding with the SHA prefix of Linux's initial Git commit
short_description: A Linux developer demonstrated how 12-character commit SHA prefixes can collide, risking tool failures. He created a collision to test the robustness of existing systems, warning about future risks if shorter hashes remain in use.

headline: A Tour of WebAuthn
short_description: WebAuthn enables strong, phishing-resistant authentication using public-key cryptography, with credentials stored on devices or security keys. It supports discoverable passkeys, user verification, and extensions like credProtect. Compatibility spans browsers, mobile platforms, and native APIs, facilitating seamless, passwordless sign-ins while emphasizing security, privacy, and flexible deployment options.

headline: Sequoia PGP: A Sapling Matures: Meet sq 1.0
short_description: Sequoia PGP has announced the stable release of version 1.0 of sq, a command-line tool for working with OpenPGP artifacts. The tool emphasizes usability, security, and comprehensive key management, with notable features like a decentralized PKI and automatic certificate recording, supporting secure encryption, signing, and verification workflows.

headline: Far From Random: Three Mistakes From Dart/Flutter's Weak PRNG
short_description: Multiple security flaws in Dart/Flutter stem from the use of insecure, non-cryptographically secure PRNGs with only 32-bit seeds. These vulnerabilities enabled practical brute-force attacks on Proton Wallet’s recovery phrases, encryption keys, and developer tools, risking user data, wallet access, and potential privilege escalation.

headline: Dual_EC_DRBG with Justin Schuh and Matthew Green
short_description: The debate over Dual_EC_DRBG's backdoor potential remains heated, with experts noting the algorithm's structural vulnerabilities and possible NSA involvement in standardization. While some argue it was a deliberate backdoor, others believe it was an internal mistake, highlighting ongoing distrust in cryptographic standards and standards bodies.

headline: AES-GCM and breaking it on nonce reuse
short_description: Reusing nonces in AES-GCM enables attackers to recover the GHASH key H and the keystream, allowing them to forge authentication tags and decrypt ciphertexts. This vulnerability underscores the critical importance of unique nonces for secure encryption and authentication.

headline: Beyond Bcrypt
short_description: In 2024, bcrypt remains a widely used password hashing algorithm, but recent discussions highlight its limitations, such as 72-character truncation and potential vulnerabilities. Experts recommend pre-hashing with HMAC-SHA512 before bcrypt to improve security, though debates continue over its proper implementation and future use in platforms like WordPress.

headline: Key Transparency and the Right to be Forgotten
short_description: The article discusses implementing GDPR-compliant data erasure in decentralized key transparency systems using cryptographic techniques like crypto-shredding, Argon2id commitments, and secure encryption. It explores technical approaches to balance transparency, security, and user privacy while addressing legal ambiguities around data deletion on distributed ledgers.

headline: For the first time ever researchers crack RSA and AES data encryption
short_description: Chinese researchers have demonstrated that D-Wave’s quantum annealing computers can crack RSA and AES encryption, raising concerns about the security of current cryptographic systems. This breakthrough suggests quantum computers are closer than anticipated to threatening data privacy, underscoring the urgent need for quantum-resistant encryption solutions.

headline: Nothing-up-my-sleeve number
short_description: Nothing-up-my-sleeve numbers are constructed to appear random and transparent in cryptography, used for generating cryptographic constants. However, experts warn that their use does not guarantee security, as backdoors can still be inserted through complex parameter choices, exemplified by NSA-designed constants and flawed algorithms.

headline: Hyper-encryption [Provably unbreakable hyper-encryption in the limited access model]
short_description: Hyper-encryption, developed by Michael Rabin, offers provably unbreakable security using public random bits and a shared secret key within the bounded-storage model. It is highly energy-efficient and theoretically unbreakable, even against future adversaries with unlimited computational power.

headline: Protecting Signal Keys on Desktop
short_description: Researchers propose using hardware security keys like YubiKey to protect Signal Desktop’s cryptographic keys from malware and privilege escalation attacks. By integrating hardware modules, they aim to secure private keys and improve overall desktop app security, addressing current vulnerabilities in key management.

headline: Big Problems From Big IN lists with Ruby on Rails and PostgreSQL
short_description: Web developers using Ruby on Rails often encounter performance issues with large IN clause queries caused by big lists of values. Alternatives like join operations, using ANY with arrays, VALUES clauses, or temporary tables can improve efficiency. PostgreSQL plans to enhance handling of such queries in upcoming versions.

headline: Indexing Hackage: Glean vs. hiedb
short_description: Meta's Glean system was tested as a flexible, faster alternative to hiedb for indexing Hackage packages. Glean demonstrated significantly faster indexing times, smaller database sizes, and efficient query performance, highlighting its potential for advanced code analysis and IDE integration, though full feature support and incremental updates are still in development.

headline: Making Postgres distributed with FoundationDB
short_description: Researchers have developed pgfdb, an experimental open-source extension that transforms Postgres into a distributed database atop FoundationDB, combining Postgres compatibility with FoundationDB’s scalability and resilience. The project is still in early stages, and performance remains to be tested.

headline: Root Cause Analysis: PostgreSQL MultiXact member exhaustion incidents
short_description: Metronome's recent outages were caused by PostgreSQL's hidden limit on MultiXact member space, which was overwhelmed during high write loads from database migrations and backfill processes. Emergency vacuums took hours to complete, temporarily halting write operations across their platform. The incident has prompted improved monitoring and database tuning measures.

headline: Litestream: Revamped
short_description: Litestream has received major updates, including improved point-in-time restores and a new VFS-based read-replica layer that fetches data directly from S3-compatible storage. These enhancements aim to make SQLite-based applications more resilient and easier to deploy at scale without disrupting existing code.

headline: Kicking the Tires on CedarDB's SQL
short_description: CedarDB, a new Postgres-compatible database spun out of TUM research, demonstrates advanced query decorrelation and complex plan structures, including DAG plans and CTEs. Early tests reveal promising optimization features, though some bugs and assertions have been noted, with ongoing experimentation planned.

headline: “Serverless” Postgres Clustering
short_description: Neon Database introduces "serverless" Postgres clustering, enabling scalable, on-demand database management without traditional server infrastructure, aiming to simplify deployment and improve flexibility for developers.

headline: OpenVMS x86 Database Modernization with Mimer SQL and Amazon EC2
short_description: AWS showcases how to modernize legacy Oracle Rdb databases on OpenVMS x86 by migrating to Mimer SQL and deploying on Amazon EC2 with high availability, leveraging AWS storage and automation services for backup, transfer, and failover. This approach enables seamless platform transitions and scalable cloud integration.

headline: The fastest Postgres inserts
short_description: Hatchet's recent benchmarks reveal that optimizing Postgres inserts through connection pooling, batching, and the COPY command can boost throughput from 2k to over 90k writes per second, significantly reducing latency. Proper tuning of batch size and flush intervals is key to balancing performance and responsiveness.

headline: A Survey of Database TLS Libraries (2022)
short_description: A 2022 survey reveals OpenSSL remains the dominant TLS library in databases, despite security concerns, with some opting for alternatives like GnuTLS and LibreSSL. Developers recommend using native or provider-specific TLS implementations for better security and performance.

headline: Xata: Postgres with data branching and PII anonymization
short_description: Xata has developed a new PostgreSQL platform that offers instant copy-on-write branching, data anonymization, and cloud-agnostic deployment, aiming to improve scalability, security, and cost-efficiency for enterprise and developer use. The platform leverages distributed NVMe storage and standard Postgres, with flexible deployment options including on-premises.

headline: Getting AI to write good SQL: Text-to-SQL techniques explained
short_description: Google Cloud advances text-to-SQL tech with Gemini models, enabling natural language to generate accurate SQL queries. They employ techniques like semantic retrieval, disambiguation, and validation to overcome challenges such as schema understanding and user intent, boosting productivity for data analysts and developers.

headline: A Ledger In PostgreSQL Is Fast
short_description: A PostgreSQL-based ledger called pgledger demonstrates high performance, achieving over 10,000 transfers per second on a local machine and over 1,600 on a cloud-hosted database. The implementation is simple, with potential for further optimization, making it suitable for most financial applications.

headline: Repair Time Requirements to Prevent Data Resurrection in Cassandra & Scylla
short_description: To prevent data resurrection in Cassandra and ScyllaDB, repairs must be completed within the gc_grace_seconds window. Running frequent, consecutive repairs—ideally every few days—ensures tombstones are consistently propagated and expired data does not reappear, though practical constraints can complicate maintenance.

headline: FaunaDB Open Sourced
short_description: FaunaDB has been open-sourced, allowing developers to freely access and contribute to the cloud database platform, potentially boosting its adoption and community support.

headline: Databricks + Neon
short_description: Databricks has announced its acquisition of Neon, a developer-focused, serverless Postgres company that enables rapid, scalable database creation. Neon’s innovative architecture supports AI-driven database management, with over 80% of new databases created by AI agents, highlighting its growing role in AI and developer ecosystems.

headline: Good enough ten-second sum types for Postgres
short_description: Researchers develop a new ten-second sum type for PostgreSQL, involving custom enum and timestamp columns with constraints. While not perfect or fully normalized, it offers a practical solution over using arbitrary dates or default timestamps.

headline: GreptimeDB as Prometheus Long-term Storage
short_description: GreptimeDB, an open-source cloud-native time series database, supports long-term storage for Prometheus with features like unified data modeling, flexible schema, and multi-protocol compatibility. While promising for metric storage, its current architecture limits workload distribution across multiple datanodes, with plans for enterprise-level improvements.

headline: Introduction to Universal Scene Description (2021)
short_description: Pixar's USD (Universal Scene Description) is an open-source framework for scalable, non-destructive interchange and assembly of complex 3D scenes. Widely adopted in film and animation pipelines, USD enables collaborative workflows, detailed scene composition, and supports extensions for custom schemas and formats, though it does not include rigging or execution behaviors.

headline: Implementing State Machines in PostgreSQL (2017)
short_description: The article details implementing finite-state machines in PostgreSQL to manage order workflows, ensuring data integrity and enabling advanced analytics. Using custom functions, aggregates, and triggers, it demonstrates how to enforce valid business processes and analyze order states over time.

headline: PostgreSQL 18 Beta 1 Released
short_description: PostgreSQL 18 Beta 1 is now available, introducing significant performance improvements, new features like virtual generated columns, enhanced security options including OAuth authentication, and better upgrade and monitoring tools. Community testing is encouraged ahead of the final release expected in September/October 2025.

headline: SQLite Extension Hub
short_description: The SQLite Extension Hub offers a variety of extensions that users can search for, download, and install manually or via the sqlpkg package manager, with options to browse, star, and subscribe for updates.

headline: Waiting for Postgres 18: Accelerating Disk Reads with Asynchronous I/O
short_description: Postgres 18 introduces asynchronous I/O with new methods like worker and io_uring, delivering up to 3x performance gains in cloud environments. The update enhances read efficiency but alters I/O timing visibility, requiring changes in observability and tuning practices for optimal performance.

headline: Kangaroo: A new flash cache optimized for tiny objects [2021]
short_description: Kangaroo is a new flash cache designed for tiny objects, reducing cache misses by up to 56% compared to traditional methods. Developed through collaboration with CMU and Facebook, it combines log-structured and set-associative caches to minimize DRAM and flash write overheads, enhancing large-scale caching efficiency for social media and IoT applications.

headline: A faster way to copy SQLite databases between computers
short_description: A new method for faster SQLite database transfers involves dumping databases as compressed SQL text files, significantly reducing size and transfer time. This approach also ensures stable, consistent copies, especially for large databases, making backups and migrations more efficient.

short_description: Extreme rewriting transformed database development, as Tyler Neely discussed innovative approaches at HYTRADBOI 2025, highlighting how starting from scratch can lead to more efficient and resilient systems.

short_description: AWS's Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL 17.4 exhibits G-nonadjacent cycles and Long Fork anomalies, indicating it may provide Parallel Snapshot Isolation rather than full Snapshot Isolation. These weaker safety guarantees could lead to transaction inconsistencies, especially on read-only secondaries.

short_description: Rails' multitenancy with SQLite3 faces challenges due to connection management and API design. Recent Rails versions, especially Rails 7, introduce `connected_to` for safer tenant switching, but dynamic runtime database creation remains complex. SQLite's file-based approach makes per-tenant databases ideal for small, isolated datasets.

headline: Anatomy Of A SQL Engine
short_description: Dolt's SQL engine has evolved through multiple IR stages, enabling sophisticated query parsing, binding, optimization, and execution. The engine employs advanced join exploration, cost estimation, and plan simplification techniques, while focusing on deterministic statistics and memory reuse to enhance performance in OLAP workloads.

short_description: The DataFusion toolkit for database building now prompts users to update unsupported browsers to access its latest features, including YouTube enhancements and more.

short_description: Udi Dahan, a renowned SOA and distributed systems expert, offers in-depth consulting, training, and insights that simplify complex architecture concepts. His pragmatic approach and real-world experience have made him a trusted authority in enterprise-scale software design.

short_description: SQL Fiddle is an online platform for practicing and learning SQL, supporting multiple database types and offering real-time execution, AI assistance, and collaboration tools, all accessible via any device. It aims to help users refine their SQL skills in a supportive, web-based environment.

short_description: Observability 2.0 shifts from traditional metrics, logs, and traces to wide events as the single source of truth, enabling granular, raw data analysis. GreptimeDB, an open-source database built in Rust, supports real-time ingestion, flexible queries, and cost-effective storage, advancing modern cloud-native observability.

short_description: Discord has revamped its search infrastructure by deploying Elasticsearch on Kubernetes with smaller, resilient clusters called "cells," improving performance and scalability. The new architecture supports cross-DM search, handles Big Freaking Guilds (BFGs) with multiple shards, and ensures efficient indexing and querying across large volumes of messages.

short_description: Vortex introduces a flexible, extensible columnar file format optimized for high performance and evolving research. Featuring minimal footer specifications, edition-based features, and support for custom encodings and layouts, it aims to stay at the cutting edge of data storage and processing.

headline: Abusing DuckDB-WASM by making SQL draw 3D graphics (Sort Of)
short_description: A developer built a primitive 3D game engine in the browser using DuckDB-WASM, leveraging SQL queries for rendering, game logic, and collision detection. Despite numerous challenges with WASM loading, SQL dialects, and async timing, the project demonstrated SQL's surprising versatility beyond data analysis, achieving 6-7 FPS in a text-based Doom clone.

headline: ClickHouse gets lazier (and faster): Introducing lazy materialization
short_description: ClickHouse introduces lazy materialization, a new optimization that delays reading large columns until needed, resulting in up to 1,576× faster query performance and significantly reduced memory usage. When combined with indexing and PREWHERE, it dramatically accelerates complex analytical queries on big datasets.

short_description: Datomic's features like as-of and speculative writes don't naturally combine, making it impossible to fork the past with current tools. A workaround using custom filtering has been attempted but fails due to internal inconsistencies, leading developers to explore alternative testing methods with partial graph extraction from production data.

headline: Start with a clean slate: Integration testing with PostgreSQL
short_description: A developer shares a solution for speeding up PostgreSQL integration tests in large monoliths by automatically tracking and cleaning only accessed tables with triggers and functions. Developers can create custom transaction layers to enhance consistency and atomicity, highlighting the flexibility and importance of transaction protocols in system design.

short_description: Researchers explore various transactional system architectures, detailing how steps like execution, ordering, validation, and persistence can be decomposed and reordered. Different designs, from optimistic to deterministic, impact performance, contention, and consistency, demonstrating a vast landscape of possible database implementations.

short_description: The article advocates for storing diverse data types—social media archives, source code, Chinese characters, or sensor logs—directly in PostgreSQL. It highlights how simple, unstructured storage combined with PostgreSQL’s indexing and JSON support can streamline data management, flexibility, and analysis without overcomplicating schema design.

short_description: sqlc-dev/sqlc enables developers to generate type-safe code directly from SQL queries, streamlining database interactions and reducing errors in application development.

short_description: PostgreSQL is essentially just a file-based system, and understanding its components—files, processes, configs—can simplify development, debugging, and workflows. By manually managing data directories and settings, users gain greater control and confidence, making PostgreSQL less of a black box, especially for local testing and prototyping.

headline: Reproducing Hacker News writing style fingerprinting
short_description: Redis now supports vector sets in version 8 RC1, enabling advanced style and text analysis. Using cosine similarity and z-score normalization, users can identify similar writing styles or detect fake accounts, with tools like Redis vectors and new scripts streamlining the process.

short_description: The developer forked ClickHouse into Ursa to enhance performance, implementing features like physical string storage, partitioned group-by, runtime indexes, and late materialization, achieving up to 80% speedups in various queries. Despite progress, further improvements like statistics, runtime indexes, and executor optimization remain in development to make Ursa the fastest analytical database.

short_description: New advancements in database durability include support for atomic multi-block writes via Linux RWF_ATOMIC, enabling true in-place atomicity for data up to 8KB. headline: Visualizing Financial Data with DuckDB And Plotly
short_description: A new approach combines DuckDB and Plotly in Python to visualize financial data from spreadsheets like Tiller. This method enables interactive, detailed charts such as sunburst diagrams, offering users powerful tools for financial insights through simple scripting.

short_description: Fast charging continues to evolve with standards like USB PD, Qualcomm Quick Charge, and proprietary protocols such as SuperVOOC and SCP. short_description: RFC 5081 proposes extensions to TLS for using OpenPGP keys in authentication, enabling TLS clients and servers to support OpenPGP certificates alongside X.509, with mechanisms for certificate negotiation and transmission.
